description: A young man in a village in Calabria, southern Italy, in 1900. Stay, go to New York, or go to the mines and railroads of the American West. Detailed context 1900-1924 (Immigration Act of 1924 ends the era); later years are simplified. Personal story, not a model of the whole population.
units: Money in units, not dollars or lire. 20 units = basic costs of one ordinary year at home prices; each place has its own cost of living. Savings are not capped.

profile.family: parents and siblings in the village

west.label: Mines and railroads in the West

parameter_status: Every coefficient is the author's assumption. Sources support the historical context and give anchors to compare against (for example the share of migrants who returned), not these probabilities.

sources.supports: Ellis Island opened on 1 January 1892; about 2% of arrivals were deported
1907 peak year (1.2 million examined); 1914-1918 war decline; 1924 National Origins Act
1880-1914: 13 million Italians emigrated, 4 million to the US, 3 million of them in 1900-1914, mostly from southern Italy; 'birds of passage'; 16.5 million Americans report Italian ancestry (2020)
1861-1985: about 35% of Italian emigrants returned to Italy
28 December 1908, Sicily and Calabria, around 120,000 dead
General mobilization 22 May 1915; about half a million Italian soldiers died
Homestead Act: age 21+ or head of household, immigrants who declared intent to become citizens could claim 160 acres
Italy: 5,615,000 mobilized; 650,000 killed and died; 947,000 wounded

calibration: v0.3 (03.11.2026): calibrated with analysis/calibrate.py to historical anchors, not to a storyline. Targets: about 35% of emigrants returned (Italian diaspora 1861-1985); about 2% deported at Ellis Island; Italy WWI: 650,000 dead and 947,000 wounded of 5,615,000 mobilized (11.6% and 16.9%). v0.1 -> v0.2: returns lowered, New York wages raised; v0.2 -> v0.3: return chances, war death and wound rates fitted.
